title: request_termination plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `request_termination` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component RequestTerminationConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

RequestTerminationConfig.description: Plugin: request_termination — Returns a canned response without proxying to the backend. The response body and `content-type` are rendered once at construction time so the request hot path is allocation-light. Useful for maintenance windows, mocking, or path/header-based short-circuiting. Runs after CORS so browser preflight responses are still emitted correctly. HTTP-family only. Configuration must be an object; unknown top-level and trigger keys are rejected. Null/scalar/array configs and explicit null property values are rejected; omit optional properties to select their defaults. Native gRPC (`application/grpc` on H2/H3) is terminated as a mapped trailers-only error: HTTP 200, `content-type: application/grpc`, a nonzero `grpc-status` from the gateway HTTP-to-gRPC map, and no DATA body. A configured HTTP 2xx does not mock a successful RPC (`200` maps to INTERNAL / 13). `grpc-message` is derived from the canned body text, not returned as RPC DATA. gRPC-Web uses browser framing rather than the configured body. WebSocket support applies to the handshake only. The plugin runs in `on_request_received` at priority 125, before authentication, authorization, IP restriction, rate limiting, and the WAF, so a termination (including a configured 2xx mock) is served without authenticating the caller or counting against rate limits; use `response_mock` (a `before_proxy` plugin that runs after authentication) for authenticated mocking.

status_code.description: Final HTTP status code returned for ordinary HTTP. Must be an integer from 200 to 599, including JSON numbers with a zero fractional part (for example 503.0); informational statuses (including 101) and out-of-range values are rejected at construction rather than coerced. Statuses 204, 205, and 304 force an empty body. A configured 2xx status never establishes a CONNECT/Extended CONNECT tunnel — those requests fail closed with 403. Native gRPC ignores this as a wire HTTP status and maps it to `grpc-status` under HTTP 200; 503 maps to UNAVAILABLE (14) and unmapped codes including 200 map to INTERNAL (13).

content_type.description: `Content-Type` header value for ordinary HTTP. Every character must be visible ASCII, space, or HTAB (runtime construction refuses obs-text and control bytes exactly as this schema does); surrounding spaces and tabs are trimmed and the result must be nonempty. The default-body renderer classifies the media subtype exactly as `json`/`xml` or an RFC 6838 structured suffix (`+json`/`+xml`) after stripping parameters — not by arbitrary substring match (so `application/notjson` is plain text). JSON types pass a valid JSON `message` through as the body and fail safe to the `{message,status_code}` envelope when it is not; XML and other types keep their envelope or plain-text renderers. Native gRPC responses overwrite this with `application/grpc`.

body.description: Explicit response body. When the field is present — including an explicit empty string — it is returned verbatim and `message` is ignored. Omitting the field selects the default renderer built from `message`. Must be empty or omitted for statuses 204, 205, and 304. Native gRPC does not send these bytes as RPC DATA.

message.description: Used to build the default body when `body` is omitted. JSON media types (`json` or `+json` after parameter stripping) emit a complete, unambiguous JSON `message` as the response body — the parsed value, compactly serialized, not string-escaped inside an envelope. Objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null all pass through this way. Malformed JSON, duplicate object member names, and other parser-ambiguous documents fail safe into the legacy `{"message":...,"status_code":...}` envelope so the response stays valid JSON and construction never panics. XML media types wrap the message in `<message>` (XML 1.0 character validation/escaping); other types emit `message` as plain text. JSON escaping of envelope string slots is applied automatically; XML-invalid control characters in `message` are rejected when XML rendering is selected.

headers.description: Extra response headers for the canned response, for example `Retry-After` on a 503 maintenance page or `Cache-Control: no-store` so downstream caches do not keep serving it. At most 32 entries. Names must be HTTP field-name tokens and are case-insensitive (two spellings of one name are rejected at construction); they are emitted lowercase. Values are visible ASCII with interior spaces/tabs, no leading or trailing whitespace, at most 4096 bytes. Refused names: protocol-managed hop-by-hop and framing fields (`Connection`, `Content-Length`, `Keep-Alive`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Connection`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Upgrade`); `Content-Type` (use `content_type`); credential and challenge fields (`Set-Cookie`, `Set-Cookie2`, `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `WWW-Authenticate`, `Authentication-Info`, `Proxy-Authentication-Info`); and gateway-owned fields (`X-Gateway-Error`, `X-Gateway-Upstream-Status`, and the `X-Ferrum-*` and `grpc-*` families). The fail-closed `403` for a 2xx CONNECT/Extended CONNECT termination does not carry these headers. Native gRPC still answers trailers-only with `content-type: application/grpc`.

trigger.description: Optional trigger condition. Without a trigger every request on the proxy is terminated (maintenance-mode default). Set only one of `path_prefix` or `header`; configuring both is rejected. Unknown nested keys are rejected. When `trigger` is present it must contain exactly `path_prefix`, or `header` with optional `header_value`; an empty trigger and a detached `header_value` are invalid.

path_prefix.description: Only terminate when the canonical request path starts with this prefix. Must start with `/`, or be exactly `*` to match the asterisk-form target of a server-wide `OPTIONS *` request (which only reaches the plugin on a route that matches that target, such as a host-only or regex route; prefix listen paths never match `*`), and contain no control characters (C0, DEL, or C1), query delimiter (`?`), fragment delimiter (`#`), literal space, `<`, `>`, or backtick; any other value can never match a parsed `Uri::path()`. Literal `"`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `|`, and UTF-8 are reachable and admitted. The prefix must also already be a canonical policy path: request paths are canonicalized at the frontend boundary (percent-escapes of characters that are legal literally in a path are decoded, and every other escape — separators, double encodings, control characters, invalid escapes, and escapes of bytes outside that decode set such as `%20` or `%7B` — is rejected with `400`, as are dot segments and backslashes in either spelling). No percent escape, literal `\`, or literal `.`/`..` segment can appear in a canonical path, so a prefix such as `/%61dmin`, `/api%2Fadmin`, `/api%20name`, `/api/../admin`, `/a?b`, `/api name`, or `/api\admin` is rejected at admission rather than silently never matching. A `.` inside a segment is fine. See `docs/request_path_canonicalization.md`. Mutually exclusive with `header`.

header.description: Only terminate when this request header is present on any raw field line (including non-UTF-8 values). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the result must be a nonempty HTTP field name (RFC 7230 token). The comparison is case-insensitive on the header name. Mutually exclusive with `path_prefix`.

header_value.description: Optional exact value for `header`. Empty (default) matches presence of any field line. A non-empty value must be a legal HTTP field value (no control character other than HTAB) and not only whitespace; surrounding spaces/tabs are trimmed. It matches when any individual field line's RFC 9110 field value (the line with surrounding spaces/tabs stripped, so HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 compare identically) equals it exactly — never against a comma-folded multi-line serialization.
